notebook: PLAN: Build a direct-sequence tree, first separating C5- from C6+, then split each branch into high-value pure products/blends. Step 1: assess feed split and column economics. Use moderate-high stages/reflux initially, then trim costs. Likely keep C3, C4, C5 as blends unless pure recovery pays.

note: Test a complete blend-oriented skeleton with moderate column severity, plus an easy pure 2,2-dimethylbutane draw.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a direct-sequence tree: C5-/C6+, then C3/C4/C5 blends and C6/C7+; recover easy pure 2,2-dimethylbutane. Step 2: test a seven-column skeleton at moderate settings, inspect recoveries and costs, then prune low-value branches and improve high-value C5/C6 separations.
Turn 1: root 80/5/5 cost $296M and gave no products; excessive settings. Turn 2 uses 35-55 stages and RR 2.5-3.2. T chain: T splits C5 bottoms; TT splits C4 bottoms; TTT removes ethane so C3 mix can sell. B removes C7+; BT attempts pure 2,2-DMB tops. C6 naphthene/paraffin split is difficult (n-hexane/MCP only 3 K apart), so avoid it initially.

note: Correct the systematically low distillate rates with higher boil-up, while reducing reflux and pressure drop to control cost; retain only the useful blend cuts.
notebook:
PLAN: Use a blend-oriented direct tree: root C5-/C6+, light branch C5/C4/C3, heavy branch C6/C7+ then paraffin/naphtha. Step 3: correct every cut by raising boil-up relative to reflux; make ethane rejection tops small; test whether C5/C6 blend revenues cover expensive duties.
Turn 2 showed all main cuts were much too heavy in bottoms: root tops 1076 vs target 1559; T tops 444 vs 664; TT tops 195 vs 320; B was actually cutting within C6, not C6/C7+. TTT C3 blend already sells. Ideal sale values are about C5 blend $172M, C4 $52M, C3 $25M, C6 paraffin $311M, C6 naphthene $94M. Avoid pure-product ambitions until blend cuts converge. Pressure drops reduced to limit refrigeration cost.

note: Sharpen the root and C5 split, while shifting the heavy-branch cuts upward to recover the valuable C6 blends; enlarge the C3 distillate as well.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a blend-oriented direct tree: root C5-/C6+, light branch C5/C4/C3, heavy branch C6/C7+ then paraffin/naphthene. Step 4: sharpen all main splits and move B/BT distillate rates toward their large blend targets; then prune uneconomic branches.
Current root recovery is close but leaks C6 into C5. T bottoms C5 blend is only 84%; TTB C4 mix 87%; B and BT distillates are far below C6 and paraffin targets. Blend values are large: TB about $529M/yr and BTT about $486M/yr at current recoveries. Raising BT boil-up strongly is essential because its target top/bottom flow ratio is about 4, versus 0.87 now. TTT also needs a much larger distillate to make a clean C3 cut.

note: Concentrate on the three valuable blend cuts, using stronger boil-up to fix recoveries while materially reducing capital and reflux costs; remove the uneconomic C3 branch.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a profitable four-column blend tree: root C5-/C6+, T makes C5/C4, B makes C6/C7+, BT makes paraffin/naphthene. Step 5: correct recoveries with much higher boil-up and reduce stages/reflux to attack the very large costs; prune low-value C3 separation.
Only TTB currently sells ($124M). TB C5 is 84% because C4 leaks down, BTT paraffin 84% because its distillate is too small. T and especially BT need larger distillates. C3 is only ~$48M and ethane contamination needs another column, so prune TTT. Main blend revenues are potentially ~$1.39B; target total column cost below ~$450M.

note: Prune the low-value light column and retune the four-column blend plant for on-spec C5 and C6 paraffin products at lower capital and refrigeration cost.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a profitable four-column blend tree: root C5-/C6+, T makes C5/C4, B makes C6/C7+, BT makes paraffin/naphthene. Step 6: get both valuable blends on-spec with stronger boil-up while cutting capital and refrigeration; C3/C4 remains unsold.
Five columns cost $687M and sold nothing. TB was 78% C5 and BTT 86% paraffin; both need larger, cleaner distillates. C3/C4 separation is low value and was pruned. Try root 45/2/8/dp.1, T 45/2/15, B 40/1.5/8, BT 45/2/25. Potential C5+C6 revenue ~$1.4B; target cost well below this.

note: Monetize the light branch with C3/C4/C5 blend splits, while adjusting the two C6 cuts to reach blend purity.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a profitable blend tree: root C5-/C6+, T makes C6 paraffin, TT/TTB recover C3, C4 and C5 blends, B/BT recover heavy blends. Step 7: monetize the large light stream and sharpen both paraffin cuts.
TB is already 93% C6 paraffin and close to a $470M/yr sale; raising T boil-up slightly should remove residual C5. BT boil-up 25 takes 89% overhead and cannot make a clean paraffin cut, so reduce to 12. TT is 1679 mol/s of valuable C3-C5 material: split C3 overhead at low boil-up, then C4 overhead/C5 bottoms. Expected blend revenue is about $73M C3, $186M C4, $619M C5, plus C6 products. Keep stages/reflux moderate because energy and capital are expensive.

note: Prune the revenue-less heavy branch and reconfigure the light train so one added column can yield both C3 and C4 blends, while sharpening the nearly on-spec C5 and C6 cuts.
notebook:
PLAN: Build a profitable blend tree: root C5-/C6+, T makes C6 paraffin, TT/TTB recover C3, C4 and C5 blends. Step 8: prune unsold heavy branch, make TT a C3+C4/C5 split, add one C3/C4 column, and sharpen C5/C6 cuts.
TB is 93% C6 paraffin, so T boil-up 18 should reject residual C5. TT boil-up 3 should keep C5 out of the light distillate; its new TTT column then splits C3 overhead from a sellable C4 bottom. TTB boil-up 10 should reject DMB from C5. Pruning B/BT saves $155M/yr of cost with no current revenue. Expected sales: about $73M C3, $186M C4, $434M C5 and $435M C6 paraffin.

note: Target the three near-spec blend families at once: slightly more C6 rejection at T, a much smaller C3 distillate at TTT, and a sharper C5/C6 split at TTB.
notebook:
PLAN: Rescue a profitable blend tree by first bringing the nearly saleable C6 cut and the large C3/C4/C5 cuts on specification; then prune or simplify any branch that remains uneconomic. Step 9: sharpen T, TTT and TTB simultaneously.
TB is already 93% C6 paraffin: modestly more T boil-up should clear 95%. TTT currently puts 117 mol/s butane in its distillate; cutting boil-up from 3 to 1.8 and adding separation should yield both C3 and C4 blends. TTBT is 84% C5 and TTBB 72% C6 paraffin; TTB needs a sharper split, so use 60 stages, reflux 2 and boil-up 13. Costs remain high, so after revenue appears, reduce severity where purity has margin.

note: Make one coordinated, aggressive purity correction: reject more C6+ at the upstream splits and sharpen the C3/C4 and C5/C6 separators so all five intended blends can sell.
notebook:
PLAN: Rescue a profitable blend tree by bringing all five near-saleable blend cuts on specification with sharper splits, then reduce severity where purity has margin. Step 10: aggressive purity correction across the train.
All revenue is currently zero. TB is 93% C6 paraffin; raise root and T boil-up to reject heavies into B. TTBT is 86% C5, with DMB and C4 leakage; sharpen both TT and TTB. TTTT is 80% C3 and TTTB 83% C4, so TTT needs much more rectification and a smaller distillate. Current cost is $654M/yr, while potential blend revenue is about $1300M/yr, so achieving specifications is the immediate priority.

note: Reject propane from the C4 bottoms and add a small ethane splitter so both light blends can be sold, while preserving the profitable heavy cuts.
notebook:
PLAN: Bring C3 and C4 blends on specification without disturbing the two profitable C5/C6 cuts, then reduce the very large root/T/TTB costs and evaluate the 91%-pure TB C6 stream. Step 11: increase TTT boil-up to reject propane from C4 bottoms and add a small ethane/C3 separator on its distillate.
Turn 10 finally valid and profitable: C5=$603M and C6 paraffin=$279M, cost=$830M. TTTT is intrinsically only 85% C3 because ethane is more volatile and cannot be removed without another column. TTTB needs propane rejection, so raise TTT boil-up from 1.5 to 2.4. New TTTT column should sell C3 as bottoms. TB is 91% C6 paraffin and remains a later opportunity; B and the lightest overhead are likely not worth recovery. Preserve TT/TTB settings because C5 is barely on-spec.

note: Add a C6-paraffin recovery column on TB to reject heavy naphthenes and capture its roughly $458M/yr blend value.
notebook:
PLAN: First monetize the 91%-pure TB stream by rejecting its heavy naphthenes, then attack the very large root/T/TTB costs without losing blend specifications. Step 12: add a moderate C6-paraffin/naphthene splitter on TB.
Current valid plant: reward 0.636, revenue 1124, cost 845. C5=$603M, C6 paraffin=$279M, C4=$186M, C3=$55.5M. TB is 91% C6 paraffin and could add about $458M revenue if a column raises it to 95%; its contaminants are mainly methylcyclopentane/cyclohexane, so a high-distillate cut should work. Preserve all existing splitters, especially barely on-spec C5. B and TTTTT remain low-value/difficult.

note: Reduce capital and reflux costs in the four expensive columns while holding boil-up ratios constant, so product recoveries and cut positions remain nearly unchanged.
notebook:
